title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 25-28 of cote 149): Grothendieck is proving the injectivity ('faithfulness') half of the anabelian Hom-conjecture. The statement is that two morphisms f, g : X -> Y which induce the same outer homomorphism pi_1(X) -> pi_1(Y) must be equal. Here Y is an 'elementary anabelian Artin variety', i.e. an iterated fibration of hyperbolic curves (in modern terms, a hyperbolic polycurve or Artin good neighbourhood with hyperbolic fibres).

On the previous page, for dominant morphisms, he reduced to the following situation. U is a dense open subset of Y, the images of pi_1(X) are open in pi_1(U), and the two maps coincide exteriorly on an open subgroup. He then states that he does not hope for a geometric proof and falls back on an arithmetic method.

This page states a Corollary. The conclusion f = g of the preceding corollary remains valid, for X normal and Y an elementary anabelian Artin variety, under any one of three hypotheses:
- (c) the image of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y) is an open subgroup (e.g. f dominant);
- (d) the image of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y) has trivial centralizer in pi_1(Y);
- (e) [struck in this form, but used next page] the centre of pi_1(X) is trivial, and the centralizers of the images of pi_1(X) in pi_1(Y) are trivial.

Justification that (c) is a special case of (d). pi_1(Y) is a successive extension of anabelian (non-abelian) free profinite groups. In such a group the centralizer of any open subgroup is trivial. The modern term is that pi_1(Y) is 'slim'. The argument: let 1 -> N -> G -> Q -> 1 with N and Q slim. If z centralizes an open subgroup H, then its image centralizes the open image of H in Q, so z lies in N. Then z centralizes the open subgroup H ∩ N of N, so z = 1.

Marginal asterisk: one must separately treat open subgroups of pi_1 of a complete curve of genus >= 2. These are profinite surface groups, not free, so slimness must be checked there too.

Reduction of (d) to (e): replace X by an 'Artin' object. Shrinking X to a dense open elementary anabelian Artin neighbourhood X' makes pi_1(X') centre-free (it is itself slim). Because X is normal, pi_1(X') -> pi_1(X) is surjective, so the image in pi_1(Y) is unchanged. Because X is reduced and Y separated, f = g iff f|X' = g|X'.

Purpose, as the next page shows: descend to a base field K of finite type over Q. Since pi_1(X-bar) is centre-free and the images have trivial centralizers, the arithmetic extensions pi_1(X), pi_1(Y) of Gal(K-bar/K) and the homomorphisms pi_1(f), pi_1(g) are reconstructible from the geometric outer data. This lets an arithmetic (Galois-equivariance) argument be run. It is exactly the use of slimness that later underlies Nakamura's and Mochizuki's arguments.
errors: The machine transcription of (c), 'image de pi_1(Y) ... sous-groupe ouvert de pi_1(Y)', must read 'image of pi_1(X) is an open subgroup of pi_1(Y)'.

In the reduction (d) => (e), the phrase 'remplacer X par un revêtement d'Artin' is probably 'voisinage d'Artin' (a dense open elementary neighbourhood). A finite étale cover would not by itself guarantee a centre-free pi_1; shrinking X to an anabelian Artin neighbourhood does, and it preserves the image since X is normal. Either reading needs this justification, which the page leaves implicit.

The slimness claim for successive extensions needs each layer slim, including the proper genus >= 2 case. Grothendieck flags this himself in the margin ('il faut aussi traiter à part...'). As written on the page, the argument covers only the free (affine) case.
Implicitly the argument concerns full profinite pi_1 in characteristic 0. The struck note on the next page shows he was aware of the issue of prime-to-p versus profinite groups in characteristic p.

ideas.what: Injectivity of Hom(X,Y) -> Hom_ext(pi_1 X, pi_1 Y) for Y an iterated fibration of hyperbolic curves, under dominance or trivial-centralizer hypotheses
ideas.modern_name: Faithfulness part of the anabelian Hom-conjecture for hyperbolic polycurves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Conjectured by Grothendieck (Letter to Faltings 1983); proved for curves by Mochizuki (1999) and for hyperbolic polycurves by Hoshi and Sawada (2010s)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983), Esquisse d'un programme (1984), as conjectures

ideas.what: Open subgroups of successive extensions of free profinite / surface groups have trivial centralizer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (centre-freeness, ca. 1990); Mochizuki (term 'slim'); Hoshi-Mochizuki for polycurves

ideas.what: Using trivial centre and centralizers so that the arithmetic extensions and morphisms are determined by the outer Galois action, enabling descent to a finitely generated field
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of extensions from outer actions for centre-free groups (H^2 obstruction / slim extensions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group theory; used systematically by Nakamura, Tamagawa and Mochizuki

ideas.what: Shrinking a normal X to an elementary Artin neighbourhood without changing the image of pi_1 or the equality of morphisms

missed.claim: Already in 1981, Grothendieck explicitly isolates the slimness of iterated hyperbolic fibration groups, with the extension argument and the separate proper-genus caveat. He uses it as the key mechanism for passing from geometric outer data to arithmetic extensions in proving faithfulness of the Hom-functor. This predates Nakamura's centre-freeness results and Mochizuki's 'slim' formalism, which are usually credited without reference to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: Comme le centralisateur d'un sous-groupe ouvert de pi_1(Y) (pi_1(Y) étant ext. successive de groupes profinis libres anabéliens) est réduit à (1)...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for slimness and the centralizer-condition formulation of faithfulness. Hypothesis (d), trivial centralizer of the image rather than dominance, is a slightly more general faithfulness statement for non-dominant maps, worth comparing with the Hoshi/Sawada results on polycurves.

deep.surprise_reason: The techniques are now standard: slimness, and reconstructing extensions for centre-free groups. But this page shows Grothendieck already formulating faithfulness for non-dominant morphisms via trivial centralizers, with the slimness-of-extensions argument, in 1981. That historical detail is not generally credited to him. There is no new theorem beyond the modern literature.
transcription_corrections: Hypothesis c): read 'l'image de pi_1(X) est un sous-groupe ouvert de pi_1(Y)', not 'image de pi_1(Y)'.
The inserted phrase 'par R est de corio[?]' is likely a garbled reading. The plausible content is 'pour Y anabélien(?) ... X normal, et'.
'revêtement d'Artin' in the last lines may be 'voisinage d'Artin'; the handwriting is ambiguous.
Item d) reads roughly: 'l'image de pi_1(X) par pi_1(f) a un centralisateur dans pi_1(Y) réduit à (1), et Y se plonge dans [une] VA [variété anabélienne/Artin] ...'.
